runtime.contract: Access includes ordinary helpers, LookupById and guarded ownership reads. Successful Access is distinct from ability Visit/entry.

runtime.gil: Free-threaded CPython3.14.6; actual GIL-off assertions at server and foreground/background SQL boundaries.
runtime.statistics: ANALYZE anchors and graph_types after setup/excluded views before first business/reset; WAL32/64MB; log_statement=none.
runtime.warmup: One excluded fresh workflow per cell; correctness cases separate.
runtime.sessions: Fresh DB/server per trial, fresh native Session per HTTP request; ordered business mutations/errors unchanged.
runtime.cache_regime: Compiler caches reused across fresh trials; OS/global caches are not flushed.
runtime.profile_reset: Fresh DB/server workflow; one reset before first business; Always admission; no across-trial history
runtime.instrumentation: DIRECT sendall-to-ReadyForQuery protocol clocks; compact native outcome callbacks and in-memory GIL callbacks. HTTP timing is instrumented.
runtime.calibration: Reviewed DIRECT driver boundary reused. Primary HTTP includes compact and GIL observer callbacks; precision and thread-CPU diagnostics have separate capture identities.

unnecessary_audit.scope: All-anchor and node denominators are separate; demand itself varies by policy. Filter-only business necessity remains unmeasured.

cpu_scope.CPU: Direct time.thread_time_ns on selected native-spawn thread, exclusive nested partition; not whole request/process CPU.
cpu_scope.wall: Direct perf_counter_ns same callable boundary. Inclusive helper wall overlaps; never sum those columns.
cpu_scope.background: Any delegated aggressive planner/payload or other thread CPU is unmeasured. Low native-thread CPU is not a totalCPU saving.
cpu_scope.remainder: native_spawn exclusive is all otherwise-uninstrumented work plus retained observation/timer overhead, not an isolated business-code CPU estimate.
cpu_scope.controls: Complete same-repeat joint selected SQL and available whole-workflow native-plan counters matched an actual n5 control. Unknown counters are not zero.
cpu_scope.timing: Separate n1 diagnostic, not pooled with primary n5. No HTTP-minus-DB CPU estimate or overhead subtraction.

precision_definitions.unit: Unique IDs per actual HTTP request and native Session nonce, summed over workflow; delivery rows also separate.
precision_definitions.demand: Successful foreground Session.get/batch_get outside the recorded planning context. Operational demand is policy-dependent and differs from a business-necessity oracle.
precision_definitions.returned_overlap: P intersection D irrespective of timing; not by itself a timely prefetch hit.
precision_definitions.service: Successful nonplanning foreground raw promotion inside a successful demand-call interval, after a non-discarded payload return of the same ID/Session.
precision_definitions.before_call: Payload-return callback precedes demand start, with later promotion-backed service; not an exact cache-insertion/readiness timestamp.
precision_definitions.late: Already materialized at actual return callback; retained independently from overlap and unused counts.
precision_definitions.white_reads: Confirmed unused returned NodeAnchor IDs Pnode minus observed successful Dnode; a lower bound. Source-validated disjoint filter-only candidates require a separate audit. _owns/jid ID reads remain valid demand.
precision_definitions.denominators: Empty denominators are null/N/A. Off returned=0 is a valid cell. Counts have n1 precision capture and are not n5 latency samples.
precision_definitions.latency: Precision pass wall/DB times are not pooled into the instrumented primary latency dataset.
precision_definitions.denominator: ALL-anchor operational successful Session demand is the default; node ratios are separately named. Demand is policy-dependent, not a business-necessity oracle.
precision_definitions.promotion_label: promoted_ids means unique promotion-backed service inside successful demand calls, not every raw promotion or generic cache hit.
precision_definitions.timely_label: timely_served_ids means payload-return callback before call start plus later actual promotion; callback is not exact cache-insertion time.
